subject: Post-call inference readout & proposed next steps for Blue Harbor
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Peña <alex.pena@blueharbor.ai>, Sara Lin <sara.lin@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call inference readout & proposed next steps for Blue Harbor

Alex / Sara — thanks again for the time today. Quick write-up while items are fresh so we have a mutual record and clear next steps.

Call summary (30 min):
- Use case: Blue Harbor will embed an LLM into real-time agent-assist and on-page summarization for sales reps (short prompts, frequent calls). Primary goal is to improve rep throughput and reduce handle time.
- Traffic profile: initial pilot ~1k requests/min with burst to 3k RPM during peak; average prompt length ~120 tokens, expected output ~80 tokens.
- SLO targets: p95 latency target 120 ms, p99 target 350 ms for single-turn generation; end-to-end (app + model) budget ~400 ms p99.
- Cost sensitivity: pilot must stay below $0.015/1000 tokens to be economically viable at scale.
- Data requirements: transcribed audio -> short prompt; no PHI, but logs retained for 30 days, SOC2 required.

Technical notes / assumptions from the call:
- Preferred model family: you mentioned experimenting with open 8B and 13B variants; we'll propose Llama-3-8b and a quantized 13B variant as fallback.
- KV/cache: strong benefit from prefix/KV caching because prompts share large overlap (agent profile + conversation context). Expect 25-40% token saving after warm cache.
- Batching: continuous batching (latency-first policy) will increase throughput; suggested max batch size 16 for 8B at your sequence lengths.
- Quantization: recommend 4-bit quantized builds for Dedicated to hit cost targets; evaluate quality with your prompt set.

Recommended deployment topology (initial pilot):
1) Redwood Dedicated pool (US-West) — 4 accelerated nodes (NVIDIA A100-class or equivalent) with 2 shard/replica strategy for redundancy.
2) Autoscaling policy: maintain baseline for steady 1k RPM, scale +2 nodes for bursts above 2.5k RPM.
3) Prefix cache on a shared KV store per-replica; warm caches during business hours.
4) Canary: route 10% traffic to quantized 13B fallback for quality check; automatic rollback if quality regressions exceed threshold.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Karthik: send sizing spreadsheet + draft topology diagram (attached) — today (attached: BlueHarbor_Sizing_v1.xlsx, redwood-deploy-topology.png).
- Alex: share 3 representative prompt/response pairs and one production traffic CSV (anonymized) — by Wed 3/31.
- Marissa: prepare a scoped Dedicated quote + SLA note referencing SOC2 and 30-day log retention — by Thu 4/1.

Open questions we flagged:
- Tokenization differences across open models affecting cost — we'll run a quick tokenization diff once you send prompt samples.
- Any latency budget constraints inside the UI (browser-side rendering) that would tighten the server-side SLO?

If this looks right, we'll schedule a technical deep-dive next week with your infra/ops folks to confirm instance sizing and networking (VPC peering options).

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call inference readout & proposed next steps for Blue Harbor

Thanks Karthik — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Our pilot target is actually 1.5k steady-state RPM (we hit ~2.8k in last-quarter peaks). I'll still send the hour-by-hour CSV you asked for.
- p99 client-side budget is tighter: our UX team needs sub-350 ms total; happy to give 50 ms to client rendering, which means server-side p99 should be <= 300 ms.
- Model preference: we want to start with the 8B family and evaluate a distilled 13B if quality gaps are too large.

I'll upload 3 prompt/response pairs and the traffic sample to the Drive link you provided by EOD Wednesday. Also copying Sara (infra) — Sara, can you confirm whether Blue Harbor prefers VPC peering (we have a VPC in us-west-2) or an IP allowlist for pilot?

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Alex
Alex Peña
Head of Product
Blue Harbor AI
alex.pena@blueharbor.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Alex Peña <alex.pena@blueharbor.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call inference readout & proposed next steps for Blue Harbor

Looping in Vivek to validate sizing assumptions and push a scoped quote. Vivek — a few engineering clarifications from the call that will change node counts:

- If server-side p99 must be <=300 ms with your described prompt lengths (120/80 avg), we should target 3 active replicas for the 8B quantized build (estimated baseline 1.5k RPM). Each replica should be able to sustain ~800 RPM p95 with batch size 12 and KV cache warm.
- For burst safety to 3k RPM, we recommend burst capacity = +2 nodes (scheduled autoscale with 0->2 warm spare instances during peak hours).
- Networking: VPC peering is preferred for Blue Harbor (lower jitter). We'll include peering setup steps in the quote; if they prefer IP allowlist, call that out as alternate.
- Observability: include token-level latency breakdown, per-route p99, and KV cache hit rate metrics in the Console dashboard.

I'll draft the quote with two options: Dedicated (recommended) and Hosted (short-term eval) with clear cost delta, plus line items for SOC2 evidence package and 30-day log retention.

Vivek — can you confirm the estimated instance type (A100 vs GA100) and whether 4-bit quantization is acceptable risk-wise for the first pilot? If we can leverage 8B 4-bit we meet the cost target; otherwise we should size for 2x the nodes with 8-bit.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call inference readout & proposed next steps for Blue Harbor

Alex / Sara — thanks for the quick confirm. Couple final items and next steps before the deep technical session:

1) Please upload the prompt samples + traffic CSV to the Drive link; we'll run tokenization diffs and a short-quality sweep on the 8B quantized build.
2) Marissa will send the formal quote (Dedicated + Hosted opt) by EOD Thu 4/1. Expect a line item for VPC peering setup and SOC2 evidence delivery.
3) Proposed deep-dive: Thu 4/7 10:00am PT — infra deep-dive with your networking and security (Sara), Marissa, Vivek, and me. If that slot works I'll send calendar invite and an initial runbook (what we'll measure, sample workloads, and gating criteria).

Quick operational note: for the pilot we recommend enabling prefix caching + token-level sampling to validate quality vs quantized variant. If quality delta < 2% on your eval set, we can default to 4-bit quantized 8B and hit price target.

If you confirm the 4/7 time, I'll book the invite and include a short pre-read (tokenization diff instructions + suggested test harness).

Best,
Karthik
